problem:

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{3}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

If the linear approximation of $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}∗ \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]),
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?

Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/47d512d278eaa912a112e96406e44d8b9a464984487e0ab9ff253a233441c2e1.png)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/4bb0fb226d008d5efe2e7a04a444a2313b2acf80f71589a2aa0a17e40246c03b.png)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1})={x}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{1},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1})=\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{2})=0,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{2})=\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/9eb84e24979469e9b1618f0a20f030963741a513292699ed4c4d342cd9d8e00d.png)

Evaluating $\boldsymbol{f}$ and its derivative at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/22f4d34b8ec830740b285e1c31954b1e382264c4f366d3ea426ecadd3fd5f5bb.png) we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/651b14a10334bdfc073b86359ce306c1b4ba25b9390f345b609978e34cc08cad.png)

The linear approximation of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf x = \mathbf a$ is given by

$$
\boldsymbol{f}\left(\mathbf x \right) \approx \boldsymbol{f}(\mathbf a) + \boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a)(\mathbf x - \mathbf a).
$$

Substituting $\boldsymbol{f}(\mathbf a),$ $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a),$ and $\mathbf a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)={x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡y,\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ e\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ e\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=3{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡y,\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=\frac{{x}^{3}}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & \frac{{x}^{3}}{y}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ e\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=1,\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}3 & \frac{1}{e}\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-1=[\begin{aligned}3 & \frac{1}{e}\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ e\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
1+3+\frac{1}{e}=\frac{4e+1}{e}.
$$
